quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slowly reduces this risk.

questions.question: When driving past a parked car on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Assume that the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, expect the door to open. Be extra careful when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road:

options.text: As long as you aren't driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and all areas of the vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When entering a crowded freeway, what should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.explanation: Speed up using the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same rights as other vehicles. It needs a full lane width to ride safely and have room to maneuver.

questions.question: When meeting a car with bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle's high beams are blinding you, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road until it passes. This protects your vision.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and watch for hazards.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers of railroad crossings. Yield to trains and never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: At night, to reduce glare from oncoming headlights, you should look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before reaching the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: The new speed limit begins at the sign. You must reduce your speed immediately.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Signal for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and easily.
questions.explanation: Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle. This lets the other driver complete the pass in less time and with less risk.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns of an upcoming railroad crossing. Watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No more dangerous than normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky and puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers in danger. Stay focused on driving to prevent crashes.

questions.question: When a bus is signaling to re-enter the road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: Yield to buses pulling back onto the road after stops. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. When safe, brake gently and pull off the road.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance between your car and theirs.
Brake hard to force them to back away.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors several times each minute to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching cars. If someone is following too closely, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-way road means that no traffic from either direction is allowed to cross the center line to pass.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are extra slippery right after rain starts.
You need more space to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it rains. Wet pavement is covered with a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down when rain is heavy or when water and slush cover the road. This helps your tires stay in contact with the pavement.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The full lane width just like other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width just like other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to ride safely. They are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not proceed unless a sign says otherwise.
